Hardy-Littlewood circle method

Words: 259 Articles: 4
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
The circle method represents a weighted additive count as an integral of products of exponential sums against a character. Near rationals with small denominator, major arcs produce a structured main term involving a singular series and an archimedean singular integral. Away from those rationals, minor arcs require cancellation bounds. The partition and approximation estimates depend on the problem; a formal integral alone is not a positivity proof.

Vinogradov's three-primes theorem (n=p1​+p2​+p3​(n sufficiently large and odd))

Words: 58
Hardy-Littlewood circle method OurBigBook.com
Every sufficiently large odd integer is a sum of three primes, with repetitions allowed. The weighted count is asymptotic to S(n)n2/2. Siegel–Walfisz theorem controls the major arcs, and Type I/II estimates for the prime exponential sum make the minor arcs negligible. Removing prime-power contributions gives genuine prime representations. This is the sufficiently-large theorem, not by itself a proof for every small odd integer.

Singular series (S(n))

Words: 60
Hardy-Littlewood circle method OurBigBook.com
A singular series assembles the local congruence densities in an additive counting asymptotic. For three prime summands it is ∑q≥1​μ(q)cq​(n)/φ(q)3, with Ramanujan sum cq​(n). Its Euler product vanishes for even n and has a uniform positive lower bound for odd n. Different additive problems have different local factors, so this is a specific instance rather than a universal formula.

Minor arc

Words: 34
Hardy-Littlewood circle method OurBigBook.com
Minor arcs are the complement of the specified major arcs. They contribute an error only when a suitable pointwise or mean-value cancellation estimate is proved; their name does not imply that their measure is small.

Major arc

Words: 48
Hardy-Littlewood circle method OurBigBook.com
In a circle-method problem of scale n, major arcs are neighborhoods of reduced rational points a/q with small denominator, where the relevant exponential sum is approximated using distribution in residue classes. For the three-prime problem one may take q≤(logn)B and ∣θ−a/q∣≤(logn)B/n, with suitably fixed B.

L-function (L(s))

Words: 342 Articles: 6
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
An L-function is an arithmetic function given initially by a Dirichlet series and often an Euler product, with analytic continuation and a functional equation in important cases. Dirichlet L-functions and L-functions of cusp forms are basic examples; p-adic L-functions interpolate suitably modified special values.

Hasse–Weil zeta function (Z(V,s))

Words: 58
L-function OurBigBook.com
The Hasse–Weil zeta function of an algebraic variety over a number field is assembled from local point-counting factors at finite places. At a good place with residue field of size q, the factor is Z(Vq​,q−s), where Z(Vq​,T)=exp(∑n≥1​#Vq​(Fqn​)Tn/n). Defining all bad-place factors requires a specified integral model or convention. The zeta function of an elliptic curve over a finite field is a local factor, rather than this global product.

Hasse-Weil L-function (L(E/F,s)=∏v​det(1−Frobv​Nv−s∣Vℓ​(E)Iv​)−1)

Words: 68
L-function OurBigBook.com
For an elliptic curve over a number field, its Hasse-Weil L-function is the product of the local factors determined by its Tate module. At a good finite place, the factor is (1−av​Nv−s+Nv1−2s)−1, with av​=Nv+1−#E(κ(v)). At a bad place use the inertia-invariant subspace and an auxiliary prime different from the residue characteristic. For a CM elliptic curve with all endomorphisms defined over the base, this factors as the product of the two conjugate Hecke L-functions.

Hecke L-function (L(ψ,s)=∏q∤f​(1−ψ(q)Nq−s)−1)

Words: 44
L-function OurBigBook.com
The L-function of a Hecke character is initially the displayed Euler product over prime ideals away from its conductor. The equivalent Dirichlet series sums ψ(a)Na−s over integral ideals prime to the conductor. For a CM elliptic curve with its endomorphisms defined over the base, its Hasse-Weil L-function factors into the two conjugate Hecke L-functions.

p-adic L-function (Lp​(s))

Words: 139 Articles: 2
L-function OurBigBook.com
A p-adic L-function is a p-adic analytic function or measure interpolating suitably adjusted special values of an L-function. The Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function is the basic example attached to a Dirichlet character.

Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function (Lp​(χ,s))

Words: 111 Articles: 1
p-adic L-function OurBigBook.com
For an even Dirichlet character χ, the Kubota-Leopoldt function interpolates generalized Bernoulli values with the relevant Euler factor and Teichmüller character adjustment. If χ=1, it can be encoded by an integral power series. For u=1+p, the p-ramified convention is gχ​(u1−s−1)=Lp​(χ,s). The trivial character requires separate treatment of the pole.
p-adic zeta pseudomeasure (∫xkdζp​=(1−pk−1)ζ(1−k)(k≥2 even))
Words: 61
Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function OurBigBook.com
On G=Zp×​/{±1}, this element of the total quotient ring of the Iwasawa algebra becomes an integral measure after multiplication by every difference [a]−[1]. Its even moments interpolate the displayed Euler-corrected zeta values. Its trivial-character component has a pole, so the pseudomeasure itself must not be treated as an element of the integral group algebra. Multiplication by the augmentation ideal removes the pole.

Linnik's theorem (p(a,q)≪qL((a,q)=1))

Words: 32
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
There is an absolute finite exponent L bounding the least prime in any reduced arithmetic progression by a constant times qL. The multiplicative large sieve inequality is one of the tools in proofs of this theorem.

Character sum (∑n∈S​χ(n))

Words: 73 Articles: 1
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
A sum of character values over a set. Arithmetic cancellation, rather than the termwise absolute-value bound, is the useful feature. A Gauss sum of a Dirichlet character is a weighted example, and the Pólya–Vinogradov inequality bounds interval sums.

Pólya–Vinogradov inequality (∣∑M<n≤M+N​χ(n)∣≪q​logq)

Words: 43
Character sum OurBigBook.com
For a primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo q, finite Fourier inversion theorem and the primitive Gauss magnitude give this bound uniformly in the interval. Bound the exponential sums by C∥a/q∥−1 and sum the resulting harmonic series. The general Gauss identity follows from the prime-power identity by the Chinese remainder theorem.

Prime sum

Words: 24
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
A prime sum is a summation indexed by prime numbers, for example ∑p≤x​1/p. The indexing restriction distinguishes it from a sum over all positive integers.

Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem

Words: 83 Articles: 1
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
For every A>0 there is B>0 such that, for Q≤x1/2/logBx,
∑q≤Q​max(a,q)=1​max2≤y≤x​​ψ(y;q,a)−ϕ(q)y​​≪A​logAxx​.
(1)
Here ψ(y;q,a) is the Chebyshev function in an arithmetic progression and ϕ is the Euler totient function. Partial summation gives the corresponding result for the prime-counting function and the offset logarithmic integral function. The theorem controls the total error over many moduli; it need not give the same bound for each individual modulus.

Weighted arithmetic-progression error bound

Words: 27
Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem OurBigBook.com
Let Eq​=max(a,q)=1​∣π(x;q,a)−Li(x)/ϕ(q)∣. For Q≤x1−η, the Brun–Titchmarsh theorem and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality give
∑q≤Q​3ω(q)Eq​≪η​(∑q≤Q​Eq​)1/2(logxx​∑q≤Q​ϕ(q)9ω(q)​)1/2.
(2)
Write each summand as Eq​​3ω(q)Eq​​, then use Eq​≪η​x/(ϕ(q)logx).

Exponential sum

Words: 918 Articles: 14
Analytic number theory OurBigBook.com
A finite sum of complex exponentials, such as S(θ)=∑n​an​e(nθ) with e(t)=exp(2πit), is an exponential sum. Cancellation in an exponential sum between its terms can make it much smaller than the sum of their absolute values.

Weyl differencing

Words: 393 Articles: 4
Exponential sum OurBigBook.com
Taking a finite difference lowers the degree of a polynomial phase. For S(θ)=∑x=1n​e(θP(x)), expand ∣S∣2 by shifts h and apply the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to those shift sums. This gives ∣S∣4≤2n∑h,l​∑x∈Ih,l​​e(θΔh​Δl​P(x)), where Ih,l​ enforces that x,x+h,x+l,x+h+l lie in [1,n]. Although individual terms can be complex, the entire sum is real and nonnegative because it equals a sum of squares. For P(x)=x3, the phase is 3hl(2x+h+l).

Weyl inequality (∣S∣≪k,η​N1+η(q−1+N−1+qN−k)21−k)

Words: 61
Weyl differencing OurBigBook.com
For a real degree-k polynomial with leading coefficient θ, k≥2, and coprime integers a,q satisfying ∣θ−a/q∣≤q−2, the displayed bound applies to its exponential sum over 1≤n≤N. Repeated Weyl differencing reduces the phase to slope k!θh1​⋯hk−1​. A geometric-sum estimate, the subpower bound for the divisor function and the reciprocal fractional-part sum near a rational complete the estimate. The arbitrary positive exponent η absorbs divisor bounds and logarithms.

Cubic Weyl inequality (∣S(θ)∣≪η​n1+η(q−1+n−1+q/n3)1/4)

Words: 65
Weyl differencing OurBigBook.com
If S(θ)=∑x≤n​e(θx3) and ∣θ−a/q∣≤q−2 with (a,q)=1, the displayed estimate holds. Twice applying Weyl differencing bounds ∣S∣4 by O(n3+n∑0<∣h∣,∣l∣<n​min(n,∥6θhl∥−1)). Group by 6hl and use the subpower bound for the divisor function. The reciprocal fractional-part sum near a rational bounds the resulting sum by O(log(2q)(n3/q+n2+n+q)). Take fourth roots, absorbing logarithms into nη when q≤n3; for larger q the trivial bound suffices. Leiden lecture notes, Section 7.2 develop this cubic differencing estimate.

Hua's lemma (∫01​∣∑x≤n​e(θxk)∣2jdθ≪k,j,η​n2j−j+η)

Words: 199 Articles: 1
Weyl differencing OurBigBook.com
For 1≤j≤k and every η>0, the displayed estimate bounds a mean value of a polynomial exponential sum. For cubes its eighth-moment bound is Oη​(n5+η). It complements pointwise Weyl differencing estimates: a ninth moment over a region is bounded by its supremum there times this eighth moment. Leiden lecture notes, Section 8.1 give the cubic formulation.
Cubic eighth-moment proof by differencing (∫01​∣∑x≤n​e(θx3)∣8dθ≪η​n5+η)
Words: 143
Hua's lemma OurBigBook.com
Write S(θ)=∑x≤n​e(θx3) and Ij​=∫01​∣S∣j. Character orthogonality gives I2​=n. For I4​, fix the difference D=x3−y3. If D=0, there are n2 choices for the two equal pairs. If D=0, any solution z3−w3=D has z−w∣D; fixing this divisor gives a quadratic equation for w, hence at most two choices. The subpower bound for the divisor function yields I4​≪η​n2+η.
The twice-differenced inequality in Weyl differencing reads ∣S∣4≤2n∑v​cv​e(θv), with cv​ counting triples (h,l,x) for which v=3hl(2x+h+l) and all four shifted arguments are in [1,n]. Thus c0​≪n2, and cv​≪η​nη for v=0: the product hl divides v, and the remaining equation determines x. The Fourier coefficients r(v) of ∣S∣4 are nonnegative counts, with r(0)=I4​ and ∑v​r(v)=n4. Multiply the inequality by ∣S∣4 and integrate. It follows that I8​≪n(n2I4​+nηn4)≪η​n5+η, after choosing the divisor-bound exponents small enough.

Power Gauss sum over a prime field (Ga,p​=p−1∑x∈Fp​​e2πiaxk/p)

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Exponential sum OurBigBook.com
For a=0 in the finite field Fp​, put d=gcd(k,p−1). The multiplicative group of a finite field is cyclic, and character orthogonality expresses the number of kth roots of y=0 as ∑χd=1​χ(y). The trivial character contributes −1, cancelling the x=0 term. Each of the remaining d−1 Gauss sums of Dirichlet characters has modulus p​, by the prime-field character Gauss sum identity. Consequently ∣Ga,p​∣≤(d−1)/p​≤k/p​.

Three power summands over a large prime field (p>k6⟹Fp​={uk+vk+wk:u,v,w∈Fp​})

Words: 40
Power Gauss sum over a prime field OurBigBook.com
For S(a)=∑u​e(auk/p), character orthogonality counts representations of x by p−1∑a​S(a)3e(−ax/p). Its zero-frequency term is p2. The power Gauss sum over a prime field bounds the other terms in total by k3p3/2, strictly less than p2 when p>k6. Every residue class therefore has a representation.

Quadratic exponential sum (∑n=1N​e(αn2+βn))

Words: 130 Articles: 1
Exponential sum OurBigBook.com
A quadratic exponential sum has a polynomial phase of degree two. Its multiplicative derivative at lag h has the linear phase 2αhn up to a constant factor. This degree reduction lets the Van der Corput inequality for finite scalar sequences reduce its size to estimates for finite geometric series.

Quadratic Weyl inequality (∣∑n=0N​e(αn2)∣≪((N2/q+N+q)log(2N))1/2)

Words: 92
Quadratic exponential sum OurBigBook.com
For coprime integers a,q with 1≤q≤Q and ∣α−a/q∣≤1/(qQ), expand the squared quadratic exponential sum by its difference h. The exponential geometric sum bound gives ∣S∣2≪N+∑h≤N​min(N+1,∥2αh∥−1). In each block of length at most q/4, the rotations 2αh are separated by at least 1/(2q): the reduced denominator of 2a/q is at least q/2, and the approximation error between two block points is at most 1/(2q). The separated reciprocal-distance sum bounds each block by O(N+qlog(2N)). There are O(N/q+1) blocks, giving the displayed inequality. For bounded q the trivial estimate supplies the same conclusion.

Vinogradov mean value (Jk,r​(Z)=∫[0,1]r​∣∑z≤Z​e(∑j=1r​θj​zj)∣2kdθ)

Words: 123 Articles: 1

Factoring local zeros isolates their poles; the remaining logarithm is controlled by disc estimates. If all zeros lie to the left of a point z in real part, their real contributions are nonnegative. Analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function to the right half-plane

Words: 49
Dirichlet eta function OurBigBook.com
The identity ζ(s)=η(s)/(1−21−s) continues the Riemann zeta function meromorphically to ℜs>0. Apparent singularities at nonreal zeros of 1−21−s are removable, as one sees by replacing 2 with an integer k for which 1−k1−s=0. At s=1, η(1)=log2 and 1−21−s∼(s−1)log2, so ζ has a simple pole of residue one.
